t: Hopper Company Queries III: Rolling 3-Month Window Averages
o: We report two averages for each of the ten 3-month windows of 2020: January-March (starting month 1) through October-December (starting month 10). For a window starting at month m we sum ride_distance over accepted rides requested in months m, m+1, m+2 and divide by exactly 3 — not by the number of rides — which is why January shows 21.00 = 63/3 despite a single accepted ride. Only requests dated in 2020 count, so the December 2019 request never joins any window. Every starting month 1..10 must appear even when its window has no accepted rides, which forces us to manufacture the ten rows instead of relying on grouped data. Results are rounded to two decimals and ordered by the starting month.
k: Divide each window total by the constant 3, not by the ride count — the average is defined over months.
Anchor rides to their request date: join Rides to AcceptedRides and bucket by MONTH(requested_at) within YEAR 2020.
A generated spine of starting months 1..10 guarantees quiet windows still appear, defaulting to 0.00.

a.i: For each spine month m, two scalar subqueries sum ride_distance and ride_duration over accepted rides requested in months m..m+2 of 2020. This mirrors the English definition line by line, making it a natural first draft; the cost is rescanning Rides and AcceptedRides for each of the ten windows. LeetCode accepts MySQL for this problem, so the same query fills every language slot.
s: Build the ten starting months with chained UNION ALL.
Per window, sum a.ride_distance by joining Rides to AcceptedRides filtered to YEAR 2020 and MONTH BETWEEN m AND m+2.
Wrap each sum in IFNULL(..., 0), divide by 3, ROUND to 2 decimals, ORDER BY month.

c.python:
SELECT m.month,
       ROUND(IFNULL((SELECT SUM(a.ride_distance)
                     FROM Rides r
                     JOIN AcceptedRides a ON a.ride_id = r.ride_id
                     WHERE YEAR(r.requested_at) = 2020
                       AND MONTH(r.requested_at) BETWEEN m.month AND m.month + 2), 0) / 3, 2) AS average_ride_distance,
       ROUND(IFNULL((SELECT SUM(a.ride_duration)
                     FROM Rides r
                     JOIN AcceptedRides a ON a.ride_id = r.ride_id
                     WHERE YEAR(r.requested_at) = 2020
                       AND MONTH(r.requested_at) BETWEEN m.month AND m.month + 2), 0) / 3, 2) AS average_ride_duration
FROM (
    SELECT 1 AS month UNION ALL SELECT 2 UNION ALL SELECT 3 UNION ALL SELECT 4 UNION ALL SELECT 5
    UNION ALL SELECT 6 UNION ALL SELECT 7 UNION ALL SELECT 8 UNION ALL SELECT 9 UNION ALL SELECT 10
) m
ORDER BY m.month;

a.t: O(10 * (R + A)) — each of the ten windows rescans the joined ride tables.
a.sp: O(1) beyond the 10-row spine — scalar aggregates materialize one value per window.

a.n: Approach 2: Month Spine with LEFT JOIN Aggregation
a.i: Instead of subqueries, LEFT JOIN the spine to Rides on the window predicate and onward to AcceptedRides, then aggregate with GROUP BY. Windows with no accepted rides keep their spine row because both joins are outer joins, and COALESCE turns the NULL sums into 0. A single join-and-group pass replaces ten correlated scans and is the version you would ship.
s: Generate starting months 1..10 with UNION ALL.
LEFT JOIN Rides r ON YEAR(r.requested_at) = 2020 AND MONTH BETWEEN m.month AND m.month + 2.
LEFT JOIN AcceptedRides a ON a.ride_id = r.ride_id so unaccepted requests contribute NULLs.
GROUP BY m.month selecting COALESCE(SUM(...), 0) / 3 rounded to two decimals.

c.python:
SELECT m.month,
       ROUND(COALESCE(SUM(a.ride_distance), 0) / 3, 2) AS average_ride_distance,
       ROUND(COALESCE(SUM(a.ride_duration), 0) / 3, 2) AS average_ride_duration
FROM (
    SELECT 1 AS month UNION ALL SELECT 2 UNION ALL SELECT 3 UNION ALL SELECT 4 UNION ALL SELECT 5
    UNION ALL SELECT 6 UNION ALL SELECT 7 UNION ALL SELECT 8 UNION ALL SELECT 9 UNION ALL SELECT 10
) m
LEFT JOIN Rides r
       ON YEAR(r.requested_at) = 2020
      AND MONTH(r.requested_at) BETWEEN m.month AND m.month + 2
LEFT JOIN AcceptedRides a ON a.ride_id = r.ride_id
GROUP BY m.month
ORDER BY m.month;

a.t: O(R + A) amortized — one join pass over rides and accepted rides instead of per-window rescans.
a.sp: O(1) extra beyond the spine rows and the grouped output.

w: Pick Approach 2 in an interview or production: one join-and-group pass beats ten correlated scans and extends naturally to parameterized window sizes. Pitfalls: dividing by COUNT(*) of rides instead of 3; dropping the YEAR(requested_at) = 2020 filter so December 2019 leaks into early windows; using INNER JOIN on AcceptedRides, which silently deletes empty windows from the output; rounding before dividing. Likely follow-ups: generalize to arbitrary window lengths with a date-dimension table, or compute overlapping running totals with window functions such as SUM OVER RANGE.
